proposed.text: A steel column must achieve a 2-hour fire resistance rating using spray-applied mineral fiber protection. What minimum thickness of protection does PD 1096 require?

options.text: 12 millimeters of spray-applied mineral fiber protection
20 millimeters of spray-applied mineral fiber protection
38 millimeters of spray-applied mineral fiber protection
50 millimeters of spray-applied mineral fiber protection

proposed.rationale: Original question was already source-correct and substantive; the prior edit (source-audited-article-batch-048) was degenerate, with 1-character garbage in 3 of 4 option text fields and a nonsensical rationale. Restored the original verbatim. Original source rationale: Sec. 603 specifies metal protection (spray-applied mineral fiber or plaster) thicknesses: 12mm for 1-hour, 20mm for 2-hour, 38mm for 3-hour, and 50mm for 4-hour ratings.
proposed.explanation: The 20mm minimum for a 2-hour rating applies to the applied protection layer, measured from the steel surface. The progressive increase from 12mm to 50mm reflects the thermal resistance needed to keep steel below its critical temperature (approximately 550°C) for the rated duration.
